author: Michael Larabel
description: Google engineers responsible for the Chrome/Chromium web browser are experimenting with Flatpak packaging on Linux. They aren't yet committed to officially supporting Flatpak packages but for now are at least exploring the option...
title: Chrome/Chromium Experimenting With Flatpak Packaging

author: Michael Larabel
description: Last year a multi-kernel architecture was proposed for the Linux kernel to allow multiple independent kernel instances to co-exist on a single physical machine. Each kernel with "multikernel" Linux can run on dedicated CPU cores whole sharing the underlying hardware resources. Linux 7.0-mk2 released today with the kernel patched for this multi-kernel behavior...
title: Linux 7.0-mk2 Released For Multi-Kernel Linux With Promising Performance Results

author: Michael Larabel
description: COSMIC Epoch 1.7 is out today as the newest update to this Rust-based open-source desktop environment with development led by System76...
title: COSMIC Epoch 1.7 Released: No Longer Slow Browsing Network Filesystems

author: Michael Larabel
description: LLVM 23.1 was released today on-schedule as the first stable release of the LLVM 23 series as the H2'2026 update to this open-source compiler stack...
title: LLVM/Clang 23.1 Released With AMD Zen 6 & NVIDIA Rigel Support, Partial C++26 Support

author: Michael Larabel
description: The PorteuX Linux distribution focused on being a high performance, modular, and minimalist distro took to forking Xfce's xfwm4 window manager into "xfwm4-gl" for OpenGL compositing support. As part of that they developed a window manager / compositor benchmark for evaluating the performance and efficiency of typical operations. Their results are fascinating...
title: Wayland Found To Be "Intrinsically Faster Than X11, But Not Necessarily More Efficient"

author: Michael Larabel
description: The latest criticism of the increased burden placed on open-source software project maintainers caused by AI / LLM agents is around too many bug reports effectively causing a "denial of service" attack on project maintainers...
title: AI/LLM Usage Becoming A "Denial of Service Attack" On Open-Source Project Maintainers

author: Michael Larabel
description: With the Btrfs pull request for Linux 7.3 having delivered more performance optimizations with some ~3x and ~5x gains mentioned in specific areas, I was eager to test out the new Btrfs performance on the in-development kernel. In today's article are some benchmarks of Btrfs on Linux 7.2 stable compared to Linux 7.3 Git with some very enticing performance gains confirmed in various workloads.
title: Benchmarking Some Incredible Performance Gains With Btrfs On Linux 7.3

author: Michael Larabel
description: Apple today unveiled the M6 as their first 2nm SoC design while also introducing the M5 Ultra as their first quad-die product...
title: Apple Launches The M6 2nm 12-core CPU, Quad-Die M5 Ultra

author: Michael Larabel
description: The pull requests for the existing Paragon NTFS3 kernel driver as well as the new modern "NTFS" drivers have been submitted for the ongoing Linux 7.3 kernel cycle. Besides bug fixes, most notable among these NTFS file-system drivers are Windows System Compression "WOF" read support for the modern NTFS driver...
title: The Modern NTFS Linux Driver Adds Read Support For Windows System Compression (WOF)

author: Michael Larabel
description: The in-development Linux 7.3 kernel is marking Nova Lake Xe3P graphics as stable in being enabled by default and no longer hidden behind the "force probe" flag. While on-by-default, there still are some features that have yet to land like the DisplayPort 2.1 ALPM functionality...
title: DisplayPort 2.1 ALPM Still Being Worked On For Intel Xe3P / Nova Lake

author: Michael Larabel
description: KDE developer David Edmundson is out today with a blog post around improvements that have been ongoing for the Plasma 6.8 release in improving the KDE remote desktop experience. As part of ensuring a good Wayland experience and hitting all the needs fulfilled by X11, Plasma 6.8 is seeing improvements for its remote desktop functionality...
title: KDE Remote Desktop Experience Improving For Closing The X11 vs. Wayland Gap

author: Michael Larabel
description: Linux sound subsystem maintainer Takashi Iwai of SUSE submitted all of the sound feature updates last week for the Linux 7.3 kernel. Besides the continued AI/LLM-generated patch churn, the sound code for Linux 7.3 sees a lot of new hardware support...
title: Lots Of New Audio Hardware Support In Linux 7.3
